forms.title: Even, odd, or neither
forms.skill: Even: f(-x) = f(x). Odd: f(-x) = -f(x). Mixed powers: neither.

variants.statement: Is $f(x) = x^2 + 4$ even, odd, or neither?
variants.explanation: Compare $f(-x)$ with $f(x)$: here every power of $x$ is even, so the function is even. Even means $f(-x) = f(x)$ — symmetry across the $y$-axis; odd means $f(-x) = -f(x)$ — symmetry through the origin; a mixture of even and odd powers is neither.

variants.statement: Is $f(x) = x^2 + x$ even, odd, or neither?
variants.explanation: Compare $f(-x)$ with $f(x)$: here it mixes an even power with an odd one, so the function is neither even nor odd. Even means $f(-x) = f(x)$ — symmetry across the $y$-axis; odd means $f(-x) = -f(x)$ — symmetry through the origin; a mixture of even and odd powers is neither.

forms.title: Average rate of change
forms.skill: Slope of the secant: (f(q) − f(p))/(q − p) — for x² + c it collapses to p + q.

variants.statement: For $f(x) = x^2 + 3$, find the average rate of change of $f$ from $x = 1$ to $x = 4$.

forms.title: Naming the transformation
forms.skill: Inside the parentheses moves opposite its sign; outside moves as written; minus reflects.

variants.statement: How is the graph of $y = f(x - 3) + 2$ obtained from the graph of $y = f(x)$?
variants.explanation: Inside the parentheses, $x - 3$ moves the graph right $3$ (opposite the visible sign); the $+ 2$ outside moves it up $2$. Reading the inner sign literally — left $3$ — is the classic trap.

forms.title: Writing a transformed rule
